recipes.name: Spinach Salad with Warm Bacon Dressing

steps.text: Place spinach into a large serving bowl; top with Swiss cheese, hard-cooked eggs, mushrooms, 4 crumbled strips of bacon, and almonds.

Heat olive oil in a small skillet over medium heat. Stir in shallots and garlic; cook and stir until shallots are softened, about 2 minutes. Whisk in vinegar, Dijon mustard, honey, and 2 crumbled strips of bacon until heated through; season to taste with salt and pepper.
Pour hot dressing over spinach and toss to coat.

raw_recipe.headline: Spinach Salad with Warm Bacon Dressing
raw_recipe.description: This delicious spinach salad with warm bacon dressing is loaded with eggs, mushrooms, cheese, and almonds for an impressive, restaurant-style appetizer.

video.description: Crunchy, salty, sweet and tangy, this salad delivers the satisfying textures and flavors you love in a good salad. Assembly couldn’t be easier: fill a bowl with spinach leaves, then top with hard-cooked eggs, sliced mushrooms, crumbled bacon, shredded Swiss cheese and crispy toasted almonds. Then create the distinctive dressing by cooking shallots and garlic in olive oil, then whisking in white wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, honey, crumbled bacon and salt and pepper and pouring over the salad while hot. So delicious!

review.reviewBody: I used some personalized touches...fried the bacon, onion and garlic together, saving the bacon drippings ( in place of the olive oil) and flavorings..added the other ingredients of the dressing to the fry pan, heated thru and poured over the spinach, eggs, and mushrooms.. yummy..but eat it all the same sitting...as it does not keep well.

I made it, well, almost. I didn’t have any swiss cheese, and I thought that cheese would make it heavier than I wanted. Also, I can’t imagine a spinach salad without red onion, so I added about 1/4 of a red onion, sliced very thin on a mandolin, and soaked in white wine vinegar for about 1/2 hour (soaking onions in vinegar really cuts down the sharp onion flavor, making them mellower and sweeter), and I substituted chopped walnuts for the almonds. The dressing was very good, the walnuts gave a nice crunch, and the combination of flavors was great. I’m not sure that I would ever add swiss cheese, though next time (and I’ll definitely make this again) I might add bleu cheese crumbles.

Great recipe. I prefer to use Turkey Bacon so I did not add sodium, as it is relatively salty. I only used two strips diced, none on top. Again, pretty salty with the bacon. I discovered I did not have White White Vinegar so I substituted 2 tsp Rice Wine Vinegar, 1/3 cup Sauvignon Blanc, and cut the Honey in half to keep the bite of the Dijon. I made the dressing in the bacon pan! Marvelous!! Thank you for the recipe!

I’ve made a version of this for years. Perfect for any time or occasion. That being said…I advise changes. As already mentioned, quickly cook shallots and garlic in the bacon drippings. save the drippings and use instead of olive oil. Dial way back on the prepared mustard and add some powdered mustard. I also agree that the dressing ingredients should all be heated together before pouring over the spinach. Omit the cheese. Wholly unnecessary and doesn’t contribute to the flavor. Also, you don’t need a whole hard-cooked egg per person unless the salad is a main dish. I would add a sprinkling of chopped pecans or sliced almonds.

I thought this was a very good recipe but as always I make alterations. I couldn't understand why use olive oil when making a bacon dressing, I cooked 6 slices and used the bacon drippings for the dressing, and it was incredible. The rest with the dijon, white wine vinegar and honey all worked very well with the garlic stir fried into the bacon and whisked the other sauce ingredients and it was so tasty. My husband said I could sell it. I did omit the almonds, which I am allergic to, but I'd not have used them anyway, and I used mozza not swiss, because I didn't have swiss on hand. I had no shallots so used two fresh cloves of garlic, and poured over fresh same day spinach and local, it doesn't get any better. I rated it 4 because of the olive oil, made no sense to me.

The family loved it. We combined the dressing ingredients (except I substituted the wine vinegar with white cooking wine)in the same skillet we cooked the bacon, using some of the residual drippings. We heated the dressing until it thickened; which took about 5 minutes. The dressing clung to the salad better and tripling the mustard, wine, and honey made enough for our family of five. Will definitely serve it again, and book marked it!

This is one of those no-fail salad recipes that holds up well to additions/substitutions or omissions. For instance, I used parmesan, real bacon bits and subbed vidalia onion for the shallot. I also used rice wine vinegar, added craisins and toasted pecans, as well as omitted the mushrooms. I'd suggest plating individual salad portions and pouring the dressing into each serving to avoid a soggy, wilted mess. I refrigerated the leftover dressing until the following day and tossed it into a wild rice dish for extra flavor. I love this salad and any remaining dressing can be repurposed too -- a win-win!

This would have been 5 stars... first I double it except for the mustard. Who doesn't like having a little left over. I use the bacon drippings to cook the onions and garlic. I also use rice vinegar. We really love it.

I will definitely be making this salad again! Turned it into a main course by adding grilled chicken. I also used the bacon dripping after discarding the grease to sauté the garlic and shallots. I substituted shredded cheddar cheese instead of the Swiss.

This was a wonderful & delicious salad. I changed it up a bit. I added chicken (for a more filling meal & our protein), sautéed the mushrooms & then added the shallots & garlic, & also Gorgonzola instead of Swiss.

I made this during a heat wave here in CT. I cooked the bacon on my cast iron skillet on the grill side burner,. Come the first day of summer and I don't cook indoors at all all summer! Made everything table side! I had a half skinless, boneless chicken breast I filleted, cooked on grill with S&P, garlic, fresh tomatoes and some fresh basil in some aluminum foil to serve with this salad, PERFECT! The only thing I did diffrent was no mushrooms or almonds.
This recipe is easy to manipulate if one doesn't have the mushrooms, honey, and garlic. These I omitted. I lowered the mustard to 2 Tbsp. The end result was delicious!
This makes a fabulous salad AND if there’s any left over, sauté it up the next morning and put it in an omelet. Yum.
No cheese, no shallots no toasted almonds, still awesome salad even my husband enjoyed. Grab some hearty bread and butter and it's dinner served.

This was an excellent dressing. I made a few changes : I added blue cheese instead of Swiss cheese, I added a tablespoon of bacon grease With the olive oil, used sweet onion instead of shallots (it’s what I had), and added a couple, of cherry tomatoes
Excellent - I used the bacon grease instead of olive oil. Soooo yummy
The warm dressing is full of flavor. We added dried cranberries.
